nodes.title: Allowable base change for the KW residual problem
nodes.statement: Let ρ̄ : G_ℚ → GL₂(𝔽) be continuous, absolutely irreducible and totally odd, and F a totally real number field, unramified at p and split at p if ρ̄|_{D_p} is irreducible, with ρ̄|_{G_F} of non-solvable image if p = 2 and ρ̄|_{G_{F(μ_p)}} absolutely irreducible if p > 2 (KW II §7.6.2). An allowable base change is a finite extension F′/F that is (1) totally real; (2) soluble, in the sense that there is a tower F = F₀ ⊂ F₁ ⊂ … ⊂ F_n = F′ with every F_{i+1}/F_i Galois with soluble group; (3) of even degree; (4) unramified at the places above p, and split at them if ρ̄|_{D_p} is irreducible; (5) such that im ρ̄|_{G_{F′}} = im ρ̄|_{G_F} and ρ̄|_{G_{F′(μ_p)}} is absolutely irreducible. It is a property of an actual extension and of the restricted representation. That such extensions exist with prescribed completions is R22.1/allowable-base-change-existence, and extra splitting conditions in an application are stated there, not here.
hypotheses: F is unramified at p, and split at p if the local residual representation is irreducible; p = 2 uses non-solvable residual image, p > 2 cyclotomic absolute irreducibility.

KW II do not define 'solvable extension'. The tower form is what their uses need and what their constructions give: Langlands' base change and descent are applied one cyclic step at a time, and the field F_r of the proof of Theorem 8.4 is a tower of quadratic extensions that need not be Galois over F. A Galois extension with soluble group is the case n = 1.
For p = 2 condition (5) keeps the image non-solvable; the absolute irreducibility over F′(μ₂) = F′ is then automatic.

'ρ̄|_{D_p} is irreducible' means absolutely irreducible, as everywhere in KW II §§7–8. An unramified ρ̄|_{D_p} has cyclic image and is reducible over 𝔽̄_p, although it can be irreducible over 𝔽; read over 𝔽, Lemma 8.1 would ask for a field both split at p and making ρ̄ trivial there.

Definition 7.9 prints im(ρ̄) = im(ρ̄|_{F′}). Condition (5) is the relative form ρ̄(G_{F′}) = ρ̄(G_F), which is what the paragraph after the definition proves (linear disjointness from the fixed field of the kernel of ρ̄|_F) and what composition needs; for the fields KW II construct the two agree, since ρ̄(G_F) = ρ̄(G_ℚ).
proofSteps: KW II Definition 7.9, with the restriction maps G_{F′} ⊂ G_F ⊂ G_ℚ and the tower form of solubility.

Composition: if F′/F is allowable for ρ̄ and F″/F′ is allowable for ρ̄ (over the base F′, which again satisfies the conditions of §7.6.2), then F″/F is allowable: the towers concatenate, degrees multiply, and conditions (1), (4), (5) are transitive.
Additional splitting requirements of an application are separate from the definition.
acceptance: An extension of odd degree is not allowable.
A soluble totally real extension of even degree on which the residual image shrinks is not allowable.
A non-normal cubic extension is not allowable even if its Galois closure has group S₃: it has odd degree, and it is not the top of a tower of Galois steps.
For p > 2, Theorem 8.2 asks in addition that the allowable base change be split at all places above p.

nodes.title: Existence of allowable base changes with prescribed completions
nodes.statement: Let F and ρ̄ be as in KW II §7.6.2 (F totally real, unramified at p, split at p if ρ̄|_{D_p} is irreducible; ρ̄|_{G_F} of non-solvable image if p = 2, and ρ̄|_{G_{F(μ_p)}} absolutely irreducible if p > 2). Let S₀ be a finite set of finite places of F containing the places above p, and for v ∈ S₀ let E_v/F_v be a finite Galois extension, unramified if v | p and equal to F_v if v | p and ρ̄|_{D_p} is irreducible. Let L/F be a finite extension. Then there is a finite Galois extension F′/F with soluble Galois group such that: (1) F′ is totally real; (2) [F′ : F] is even; (3) F′_w ≅ E_v over F_v for every v ∈ S₀ and every place w | v of F′, so that F′/F is unramified above p, split at each v with E_v = F_v, and split above p when ρ̄|_{D_p} is irreducible; (4) F′ is linearly disjoint over F from L, from the fixed field K of ker ρ̄|_{G_F} and from K(μ_p), so that ρ̄(G_{F′}) = ρ̄(G_F) and ρ̄(G_{F′(μ_p)}) = ρ̄(G_{F(μ_p)}). (5) If every E_v, v ∈ S₀, has degree at most 2 over F_v, then F′ can be taken quadratic over F. In particular F′/F is an allowable base change (R22.1/allowable-base-change) with the prescribed completions at S₀. The base F′ again satisfies the conditions of §7.6.2, so the statement can be applied repeatedly, and the resulting towers are allowable over F.
hypotheses: At a place above p only an unramified E_v may be prescribed, and only the trivial one when ρ̄|_{D_p} is irreducible. A nontrivial unramified E_v above p occurs in Lemma 8.1 (to make ρ̄ trivial above p when it is unramified there), in the dyadic branch with k(ρ̄) = 4 and in type (C) with k(ρ̄) = 2, the two cases in which Theorem 8.4 does not promise splitting at p.
Evenness comes from one auxiliary place with the unramified quadratic extension prescribed, not from the places of S₀; without it F′ = F would satisfy (1), (3) and (4).

KW II's second criterion, for dihedral projective image (a prime split in the field cut out by the projective image and inert in F(μ_p)), is not needed: disjointness from K(μ_p) preserves the image over the cyclotomic field.

KW II cite Lemma 2.2 of Taylor's 'On icosahedral Artin representations II' for this; that paper was not read. The statement is derived here from Clozel–Harris–Taylor's Lemma 4.1.2, which was read and is owned here by R22.1/cht-character-extension and R22.1/cht-soluble-prescribed-completions.
No automorphic input is used: this is existence of a field, not GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer R17.4's base change.
'ρ̄|_{D_p} is irreducible' means absolutely irreducible (see R22.1/allowable-base-change).

Clause (5) matters: Lemma 4.1.2 controls the completions but not the global degree, and the proof of Theorem 8.4 needs extensions of degree exactly 2 (KW II p. 77: each F_i/F_{i−1} is quadratic, with one place above v_i's neighbours and two above v_i). For exponent 2 no class field theory is needed, only weak approximation.
proofSteps: Auxiliary place. Choose a finite place u of F outside S₀, not above p, and let E_u be the unramified quadratic extension of F_u.

Apply Clozel–Harris–Taylor's Lemma 4.1.2 (owned here by R22.1/cht-character-extension and R22.1/cht-soluble-prescribed-completions) to F, to D the Galois closure over F of L·K(μ_p), and to the set S = S₀ ∪ {u} ∪ {real places of F}, with the given E_v at S₀, E_u at u and E_v = F_v = ℝ at the real places. It gives a finite soluble Galois F′/F, linearly disjoint from D, with F′_w ≅ E_v for all w | v ∈ S.
Totally real: every real place of F splits completely in F′. Even degree: F′/F is Galois, so the local degree [F′_w : F_u] = 2 divides [F′ : F]. The conditions at p are read off (3).

Images. F′ is linearly disjoint from K(μ_p) over F, so restriction is an isomorphism Gal(F′K(μ_p)/F′) ≅ Gal(K(μ_p)/F) carrying the subgroup that fixes μ_p to the subgroup that fixes μ_p. Hence ρ̄(G_{F′}) = ρ̄(G_F) and ρ̄(G_{F′(μ_p)}) = ρ̄(G_{F(μ_p)}); absolute irreducibility over F′(μ_p), and non-solvability at p = 2, are properties of these images (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.4).

Quadratic case (5). Write E_v = F_v(√d_v) with d_v ∈ F_v^× (d_v = 1 if E_v = F_v). Choose a finite place z of F outside S₀, not above 2, that splits completely in D (Chebotarev for the trivial class; Tau Ceti Chebotarev, Layer 10), and a non-square unit d_z of F_z. The squares are open in each F_v^×, so by weak approximation there is d ∈ F^× that is totally positive, lies in d_v·(F_v^×)² for v ∈ S₀ and in d_z·(F_z^×)². Put F′ = F(√d). It is totally real, quadratic (z is inert), with completions E_v at S₀; and F′ is not contained in D, because z is inert in F′ and splits completely in D, so F′ ∩ D = F. No auxiliary place u is needed, since the degree is 2.

Iteration. F′ is totally real, unramified at p and split at p when required, with the same residual images, so §7.6.2 holds over F′; a tower of such steps is allowable over F by the composition property of R22.1/allowable-base-change.
acceptance: F = ℚ, p = 5, S₀ = {5} with E₅ = ℚ₅, u = 3: ℚ(√11) is real quadratic, 5 splits in it (11 ≡ 1 mod 5) and 3 is inert (11 ≡ 2 mod 3). Disjointness from K is a further condition, which is why D enters the construction.
With S₀ = {v | p} and every E_v = F_v the lemma gives the allowable base changes 'split at p' of Theorem 8.2.

Prescribing the unramified extension of degree m at the places of a finite set makes the p-part of the residue-field unit groups there as large as required; this is the use in the proof of Theorem 8.2 (order divisible by the p-part of 2p(4N_w)).

Over the field F_{i−1} of the proof of Theorem 8.4, clause (5) with the trivial extension at the places above v_i and the unramified quadratic extension at the places above the other v_j gives a quadratic F_i, with v_j inert for j ≠ i and split for j = i. Without clause (5) the degree of F_i could be a larger even number, and the count of places above v_1, …, v_i in the proof would be wrong.
Without the real places in S the extension could be totally complex, and the Hilbert modular setting would be lost.

nodes.title: The residual hypotheses (α) and (β) persist under allowable base change
nodes.statement: Let F and ρ̄ be as in KW II §7.6.2 and F′/F an allowable base change. If ρ̄|_{G_F} satisfies (α) with witness π, then ρ̄|_{G_{F′}} satisfies (α) with witness the base change π_{F′}; likewise for (β). More precisely π_{F′} is cuspidal, it is discrete series of the same parallel weight at every infinite place of F′, ρ̄_{π_{F′}} ≅ ρ̄_π|_{G_{F′}}, and for places w | v | p: π_{F′,w} is unramified if π_v is, and its conductor exponent is at most 1 if that of π_v is.
hypotheses: The tower form of solubility in R22.1/allowable-base-change is what is used: base change is applied along each cyclic step of prime degree.

Cuspidality of each base change uses that the restriction of ρ̄ stays absolutely irreducible (condition (5) of the definition): a cuspidal π whose base change along a cyclic extension is not cuspidal is automorphically induced from that extension, and then ρ_π restricted to it is reducible.
F′/F is unramified above p, and for an unramified local extension the conductor exponent of the local base change equals that of π_v.
The definitions of (α) and (β) do not contain this transport; KW II use it without comment whenever they 'reinitialise' the base field.
proofSteps: Refine the tower of R22.1/allowable-base-change to cyclic steps of prime degree, each Galois over the previous field and totally real.

For one cyclic step apply Langlands' base change (GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer R17.4): it exists, is compatible with local base change at every place, and is cuspidal by the irreducibility remark above.

Local behaviour. At infinite places the extension of completions is ℝ/ℝ and the weight is unchanged. At w | v | p the extension F′_w/F_v is unramified: an unramified principal series stays unramified, and the conductor exponent is unchanged in general.
Galois side. ρ_{π_{F′}} ≅ ρ_π|_{G_{F′}} by comparison of Frobenius traces at the unramified places (AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations R19.2), hence the same for the residual representations.
acceptance: F′/F quadratic, π unramified at v | p inert in F′: π_{F′,w} is unramified, so an (α)-witness base-changes to an (α)-witness.
A Steinberg component at v | p (conductor exponent 1) base-changes along an unramified extension to a Steinberg component: a (β)-witness stays a (β)-witness and does not become an (α)-witness.
If the residual image shrank over F′ so that ρ̄|_{G_{F′}} were reducible, π_{F′} could fail to be cuspidal; this is excluded by the definition of allowable.

nodes.title: Lemma 8.1: the initial totally real field
nodes.statement: For S-type ρ̄ : G_ℚ → GL₂(𝔽), with 2 ≤ k(ρ̄) ≤ p + 1 if p > 2, cyclotomic irreducibility for p > 2 and non-solvable image for p = 2, there exists F/ℚ solvable, totally real of even degree, unramified at p, split at p if ρ̄|D_p is irreducible or k(ρ̄) = p + 1, preserving the relevant residual image hypotheses. The restriction is unramified away from p, and is trivial at places above p if ρ̄|D_p is unramified. The following paragraph SUPPOSES a suitable determinant character ψ given; its existence is not part of Lemma 8.1.
hypotheses: The representation and residual image hypotheses are those of the opening of KW II §8, p. 69.
proofSteps: Local prescriptions over ℚ. At each prime q ≠ p where ρ̄ is ramified let E_q be the extension of ℚ_q cut out by ρ̄|_{D_q}, a finite Galois extension over which ρ̄ becomes trivial. At p let E_p be the unramified extension of degree the order of ρ̄(Frob_p) if ρ̄|_{D_p} is unramified, and E_p = ℚ_p otherwise; in particular E_p = ℚ_p when ρ̄|_{D_p} is absolutely irreducible or k(ρ̄) = p + 1, since ρ̄|_{D_p} is then ramified.

Apply R22.1/allowable-base-change-existence over the base ℚ, with S₀ the set of these primes. The base ℚ satisfies §7.6.2 by the residual hypotheses at the opening of §8. The output F/ℚ is soluble and Galois, totally real, of even degree, unramified at p and split at p in the two cases required, with the prescribed completions.

Unramified away from p: at a place above q the completion of F contains E_q, over which ρ̄ is trivial. Trivial above p when ρ̄|_{D_p} is unramified: the completion is E_p, which the Frobenius of order the order of ρ̄(Frob_p) cuts out.
The image hypotheses over F and F(μ_p) are conclusion (4) of the existence lemma. KW II omit the proof of Lemma 8.1; this is the construction it leaves to the reader.

nodes.title: Lemma 7.10: adjustment of determinant characters
nodes.statement: Let ψ, ψ′ be arithmetic characters with the same reduction and equal restrictions to an open subgroup of 𝒪*_{F_p}; assume their restrictions to 𝒪*_{F_v} agree for a finite set V of finite places. After enlarging coefficients, there is a finite-order p-power character ζ, unramified at V, and a totally real solvable extension F′/F, disjoint from any prescribed finite extension and split at V, such that ζ²|_{F′} ψ_{F′} = ψ′_{F′}. For odd p take the unique square root of ψ′/ψ in its p-primary finite-order character group and F′ = F. The dyadic branch needs a local-character extension theorem followed by a split extension; it is not an unrestricted global square-root assertion.
hypotheses: The ratio ψ′/ψ is of finite order, p-primary and totally even. Both local compatibility hypotheses are essential.
KW II's convention: characters of F*\(𝔸_F^∞)*, that is, idele class characters trivial at the infinite places.

KW II appeal to the Grunwald–Wang theorem (Artin–Tate, Chapter 10, Theorem 5) for p = 2. What the argument uses is the extension of finitely many local characters of 2-power order to a global character of 2-power order; no global character of prescribed exact order is needed, so the special case of Grunwald–Wang does not arise. It is supplied by Clozel–Harris–Taylor's Lemma 4.1.1 with the 2-primary projection.
proofSteps: For odd p, squaring is an automorphism of the finite p-group of characters generated by ψ′/ψ; take ζ its square root there and F′ = F.

For p = 2, fix a finite Galois L/F from which F′ is to be disjoint and a finite set W of places, unramified in L and for ψ, ψ′, whose Frobenius elements meet every conjugacy class of Gal(L/F). At v ∈ V ∪ W the character (ψ′/ψ)_v is unramified of 2-power order (the restrictions to the local units agree), so after enlarging 𝒪 it has an unramified square root ζ_v of 2-power order.

Extend. By Clozel–Harris–Taylor's Lemma 4.1.1 (owned here by R22.1/cht-character-extension and R22.1/cht-soluble-prescribed-completions) applied to S = V ∪ W ∪ {real places}, with ζ_v at V ∪ W and the trivial character at the real places, there is a finite-order idele class character with these local components; its 2-primary component ζ has 2-power order and the same local components, because they have 2-power order. ζ is unramified at V and trivial at the infinite places.

The field. ζ²ψ/ψ′ is a finite-order character of 2-power order, trivial at the real places and on F_v* for v ∈ V ∪ W. By global class field theory (Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory, Layer 12) its kernel cuts out a cyclic extension F′/F, totally real and split at V ∪ W, over which ζ²ψ and ψ′ agree. F′ ∩ L is Galois over F and split at W, so every Frobenius class of Gal(F′ ∩ L/F) is trivial and F′ ∩ L = F: F′ is linearly disjoint from L.
acceptance: For p = 2 a quadratic character has no square root in the group it generates; this is why a field extension is needed.
Prescribed splitting at V is retained, and ζ is unramified at V.

F′ = F in the odd-p argument is allowed here; this lemma does not assert that F′/F has the even degree of Definition 7.9. In its uses it is followed by an allowable base change (R22.1/allowable-base-change-existence).
The global character produced by Lemma 4.1.1 may have order divisible by odd primes; only its 2-primary component is used.

nodes.title: Theorem 8.2: minimal modular lifts in all source cases
nodes.statement: Let ρ̄, F, ψ satisfy §8.1. For p > 2 assume both α and β; for p = 2 assume β and α when k(ρ̄) = 2. Choose π as α in case (a) (β is also allowed when k = 2), β in cases (b)/(c), and α when p = k = 2 or β in the dyadic branch. Let Σ be a subset of the Steinberg places of π; if π is a β witness and k = 2, include its Steinberg places above p. (b) ψ kind (ii), k < p + 1, parallel weight 2, U₁(v) invariants above p with associated residue character factoring through norm to 𝔽_p*. (c) k = p + 1, ψ kind (ii), parallel weight 2 and U₀(v) invariants above p. For p = 2 use kind (ii), weight 2, unramified above 2 outside Σ when k = 2, and Steinberg at every place above 2 when k = 4. nodes.title: The quaternionic level-raising step for Theorem 8.4

nodes.title: Extending finite local characters
nodes.statement: Let F be a number field, S a finite set of places and χ_S: ∏_{v∈S} F_v^× → Qbar^× a continuous finite-order character. There is a continuous finite-order character χ: A_F^×/F^× → Qbar^× with the prescribed restriction. If the local character has p-power order, χ may also be chosen of p-power order. Its order may exceed the order of χ_S; no global character into a fixed group of that same order is asserted. The finite-order conclusion is a refinement of CHT Lemma 4.1.1’s printed continuous-extension statement, obtained from its proof.
hypotheses: Give Qbar^× the discrete topology for these finite-image characters. Add every infinite place to S, with trivial character at newly added places.
The finite-order refinement needs the finite-index statement for the open subgroup of idele classes; it does not assert that this subgroup is finite.
proofSteps: By the S-unit congruence-subgroup input, choose an open compact U in the ideles away from S on which the intersection with diagonal F^× has trivial χ_S. Arrange U_v=O_v^× at almost every finite place. Extend χ_S to the image H of U·∏_{v∈S} F_v^× in C=A_F^×/F^× by making it trivial on U.

H is open and C/H is finite by finiteness of the corresponding ray-class quotient, since S contains every infinite place. The extended character χ_H has finite image, so ker χ_H has finite index in C and is open. Thus C/ker χ_H is a finite abelian group.
Extend χ_H from H/ker χ_H to C/ker χ_H with values in the divisible group of all roots of unity. This gives finite image and an open kernel, hence a continuous finite-order character on C.

If the prescribed character has p-power order, project this finite-order extension to its p-primary component in the roots of unity. The other primary components restrict trivially on the local product, so the restriction is unchanged. Apply reciprocity to realise cyclic local extensions; the enlarged global order accommodates the Grunwald–Wang obstruction.
acceptance: Trivial local data admit the trivial global extension. For p=2 the global character may need higher 2-power order and extra ramification; a same-order cyclic extension is not promised.
Check that the finite quotient used is C/ker χ_H, rather than H or the local product. For local p-power characters the p-primary projection preserves every prescribed value.

nodes.title: Soluble extensions with prescribed completions
nodes.statement: Let F be a number field, D/F finite Galois, S a finite set of places, and E_v/F_v finite Galois for each v in S (at real places either R or C). There is a finite soluble Galois E/F linearly disjoint from D/F such that for every w above v in S, E_w is isomorphic to E_v as an F_v-algebra. Taking E_v=R at every real place makes E totally real when F is totally real. No assertion of cyclic E of a prescribed degree is made.
hypotheses: All hypotheses in the statement are required; the supplier interfaces below are not claims of implementation.
proofSteps: Add split conditions at a nonsplit prime for each simple Galois subextension of D, by Chebotarev.
Induct on the maximum of the local extension degrees. Finite Galois groups of nonarchimedean local fields are soluble, so choose a nontrivial cyclic quotient at each nonsplit place.
Use the character-extension lemma and global/local reciprocity to realise the cyclic local first steps; apply induction to the remaining local extensions.
Take the normal closure of the composite over F; local normality ensures the completions remain E_v, solvability is preserved, and the added split conditions force disjointness.
acceptance: For all L_v=K_v check complete splitting, and for a real place prescribed R check that all resulting real completions remain R. The avoidance field must be included at each cyclic tower step.

nodes.statement: For the avoidance problems with ζ≡1 mod λ, their local deformation conditions and coefficient characters reduce to the same data. Using the same auxiliary primes, framings, coefficient lattices and branch labels gives identifications of the two global rings and Hecke modules modulo λ, equivariant for the common scalar action. Stabilize these comparison maps together with the two patching systems, so R_∞/λ≅R′_∞/λ and M_∞/λ≅M′_∞/λ with the common local-ring action.
hypotheses: Use the coefficient, representation and level hypotheses specified in the statement.
proofSteps: The chosen root ζ reduces to one; the specified local quotients therefore have the same special fibre by the local avoidance theorem. The chosen coefficient characters and their lattices also reduce compatibly.

Apply the global quotient universal property and the equivariant finite-level coefficient comparison with identical primes and labels. Add these maps and their commuting squares to the finite structured isomorphism classes before passing to a common subsequence.

The compatible inverse limit and finite-module quotient exactness identify the two patched special fibres and modules with their common scalar action. Patching unrelated subsequences would not provide these comparisons.

nodes.title: Arithmetic realization of each finite patching level
nodes.statement: Fix a≥0 with p^a>N for the isotropy exponent; at p=2 also require a≥2. For all sufficiently large n≥m (m≥3 at p=2), put D_{m,n}=R_{n+a}/(c_mR_{n+a}+m_{R_{n+a}}^{(r_m)}) and L_{m,n}=M_{n+a}/c_mM_{n+a}. These are level-m data. The annihilator b_ℓ of M_ℓ satisfies b_ℓ⊂((1+y_i)^{p^{ℓ−a}}−1:i≤h), so b_{n+a}⊂c_m. If b is the number of generators of m_A, set r′_m=b r_m; m_A^{r′_m}⊂m_A^{(r_m)}, so every D_{m,n} is a quotient of the finite ring A/m_A^{r′_m}. The augmentation to R/(c_m+m_R^{(r_m)}) is an isomorphism after J, and the corresponding module augmentation is equivariant.
hypotheses: Use the coefficient, representation and level hypotheses specified in the statement.
proofSteps: Use Δ_Q=Δ′_Q/Δ′_Q[N] and the fixed shift a, so that reduction of M_{n+a} modulo c_m is free of rank s. The unshifted level-n bound with p^n is not available for the isotropy quotient.

A maximal-ideal element acts nilpotently on the s-dimensional residual augmentation of M_n. The nilpotence estimate in Kisin (3.3.1) gives its r_m-th power zero on L_{m,n}; thus the D_{m,n}-action is defined.

Surjectivity of the global presentation gives A↠D_{m,n}. The pigeonhole bound on b maximal-ideal generators gives m_A^{b r_m}⊂m_A^{(r_m)}, yielding a finite ambient truncation. Quotient the known augmentation kernels and retain all scalar actions.

nodes.title: Finite stabilization with all comparison maps
nodes.statement: At each fixed m there are finitely many isomorphism classes of the level-m arithmetic data, including every coefficient, presentation, augmentation and module-action map. There is a diagonal subsequence n_i and compatible identifications between the stabilized level-m data and the reductions of level-(m+1) data. The ring transition is the quotient by c_m+m^{(r_m)} and the module transition is quotient by c_m. Every coefficient, deformation and Hecke comparison square commutes. At p=2 stabilize additionally the determinant map, action chunks, embeddings and the small-kernel determinant-one comparison.
hypotheses: Use the coefficient, representation and level hypotheses specified in the statement.
proofSteps: A/m_A^{r′_m} and S∞/c_m are finite sets, so there are finitely many ring quotients, free-module action tables and structure maps of the required cardinalities. The same argument applies to the truncated dyadic action data.

At successive m choose infinite subsequences and identifications of the complete structured data, not just their isomorphism classes after forgetting maps. Diagonalize and choose compatible reductions.

Apply the owner’s cofinal open-quotient patching with scalar action through the deformation ring. The ideals contain powers of the full maximal ideal; no passage using only π-power truncations is made.

nodes.title: Realizing the dyadic action chunks
nodes.statement: Let a≥2 and 2^a>N. At level n+a, choose a compatible surjection Z^t→G_{n+a} inducing G′_{n+a}≅(Z/2^{n+a−2})^t. For n≥m≥3, put D′_{m,n}=R′_{n+a}/m_{R′_{n+a}}^{r′_m}, with its determinant map and restricted T_{2^m} action chunk. Together with D_{m,n},L_{m,n} from the shifted arithmetic construction this satisfies every enhanced level-m condition, including D″_{m,n}↠D_{m,n} with kernel in m^m. The inequality a≥2 supplies T_{2^n}⊂(G′_{n+a})*. The quotient by the full determinant character is not replaced by a fixed-determinant equality before this comparison.

Use the ordinary maximal-ideal truncation r′_m to descend the action and determinant map. The global determinant comparison gives a quotient of the determinant-one fibre whose residual kernel lies in m^m. All module/scalar compatibilities are inherited from the shifted arithmetic construction.

nodes.title: Corrected type-sensitive Hecke module
nodes.statement: For the BCDT/CDT global deformation problem over Q, let U_S,V_S and I′_S be the type level, its type kernel and the chosen Hecke ideal; r is the auxiliary prime of CDT §5.3. With the integral type lattice M_S and G_S=U_S/V_S, define L_S=Hom_{O[G_S]}(M_S,H¹(X_{V_S},O))[I′_S] (insert r if necessary). For residual support use the modified levels U′_{S,q}=V′_{S,q}=U_1(q^{c_q}) at q∈T(ρ̄), unchanged elsewhere, and L′_S=Hom_{O[U′_S/V′_S]}(M_ℓ,H¹(X_{V′_S},O))[I′_S]. The coefficient local system is the dual of the type lattice; the Serre coefficient comparison uses L_n⊗k. For an extended type enlarge U_S by w_ℓ and extend the type representation to that group, choose its invariant lattice, and form the analogous Hom-module for the finite quotient after dividing by ℓ^{sZ}. Its localized cohomological description is the w_ℓ=1 direct summand of H¹, with the matching compactly supported summand.
hypotheses: ℓ>2; O is large enough to define every local type, lattice and pairing. The residual representation is modular and absolutely irreducible on G_{Q(√ℓ*)}; its local centralizer is k. Use the exact BCDT type and admission predicates requested from Local R08.3.

The extended-type w_ℓ satisfies w_ℓ²=1 on the relevant localized coefficient cohomology. Because 2 is a unit, the invariant summand is cut out by (1+w_ℓ)/2. The type extension and central power ℓ^s are part of the input.
proofSteps: Import the modular-curve/local-system and compact-type lattice constructions from their owners. Form the displayed Hom action image and its Hecke-ideal submodule.
Use the corrected auxiliary levels in the residual comparison. Descent of invariants along V′⊂V requires V′ normal in V; all coefficient actions are continuous for the ℓ-adic topology.
For extended types use the extended compact group in every Hom and level comparison, and restrict duality, level-control and auxiliary-module maps to the + summand.

nodes.title: Type-sensitive global comparison
nodes.statement: In the BCDT global deformation problem, residual modularity, absolute irreducibility on G_{Q(√ℓ*)}, local scalar centralizer, and an admitted weakly acceptable (extended) type give the CDT type-sensitive comparison R_S≅T_S, T_S a complete intersection and L_S finite free over T_S, using the corrected module. A given potentially Barsotti–Tate lift supplies a nonzero type prime, so the zero branch of weak acceptability cannot occur. For extended types every pairing, auxiliary-level module and numerical comparison is taken on the w_ℓ=1 summand.
hypotheses: Use the coefficient, representation and level hypotheses specified in the statement.
proofSteps: Use the local weak-acceptability quotient and the actual lift to enter the nonzero acceptable branch, and use admission to obtain a nonempty automorphic set.

Apply the classical Taylor–Wiles numerical/module criterion requested from the patching owner to the corrected type module. Its hypotheses include the perfect pairing, residual injectivity of level change, congruence ideal factors and auxiliary diamond freeness, as in CDT Propositions 5.5.1/5.6.1.

For an extended type use the enlarged groups in all Hom and level-change maps, take w_ℓ=1 in compact and ordinary cohomology, identify invariants with coinvariants using ℓ odd, and retain the resulting direct summand in the freeness argument.

Use the remaining BCDT §10 label/hypothesis corrections in the local-type and numerical setup: the real group, η-character labels and patched algebra A∞. The discarded σ_n semisimplicity assertion is not an input. Elliptic-curve j-invariant consequences are outside this target.

nodes.statement: Let ℓ be odd, E/Q_ℓ finite with residue k, and ρ:G_Q→GL₂(E) continuous, odd and unramified outside finitely many primes. Assume ρ̄ is modular and ρ̄|G_{Q(√((-1)^((ℓ−1)/2)ℓ))} absolutely irreducible. Require End_{k[G_{Qℓ}]}(ρ̄)=k. If ρ|G_{Qℓ} is potentially Barsotti–Tate of ℓ-type τ, τ admits ρ̄|G_{Qℓ} and τ is weakly acceptable for that residual representation, then ρ is modular. Type includes the BCDT finite-order prime-to-ℓ determinant factor; these hypotheses do not assert lifting for every arbitrary type.

Use weak acceptability to compare the prescribed local type ring with the weak ring in the numerical argument. The corrected coefficient module and CDT criterion identify the relevant deformation ring with its Hecke action image.
The point defined by ρ therefore gives a characteristic-zero Hecke eigensystem. The automorphic Galois representation attached to it is ρ by its trace identities.

nodes.title: Kisin crystalline lifting over Q in the medium-weight range
nodes.statement: Let p>2 and ρ:G_{Q,S}→GL₂(O) be continuous, crystalline at p with Hodge–Tate weights {0,k−1}, 2≤k≤2p−1. Assume a cuspidal modular form of weight k has residual representation ρ̄, that ρ̄|G_{Q(ζ_p)} is absolutely irreducible and End_{k[G_{Qp}]}ρ̄=k. Then ρ is modular. This is the F=Q specialization of Durham Theorem (3.14), avoiding its stated higher-weight Hilbert level-lowering limitation.

nodes.title: The nonordinary weight-p-plus-one endpoint
nodes.statement: Let p>2, ρ crystalline of weights {0,p}, nonordinary at p, finitely ramified, with modular ρ̄ and ρ̄|G_{Q(ζ_p)} absolutely irreducible. In the residual Serre-weight-two branch, the BLZ calculation makes ρ̄|G_{Qp} absolutely irreducible, hence its endomorphism ring is k after choosing a splitting coefficient field. The weight theorem gives a mod-p weight-two form of level prime to p; multiplication by the Hasse invariant followed by characteristic-zero eigenform lifting gives a weight-p+1 cuspidal modular witness for the same residual representation. Thus Kisin’s Q crystalline lifting theorem applies and ρ is modular.

nodes.title: Corrected generic rank of a patched type module
nodes.statement: In the corrected Kisin §2.2 setup, with p>2 completely split in F, residual absolute irreducibility on G_{F(ζ_p)}, a nonzero modular localization and trivial isotropy, impose at v∈S∖Σ_p that 1−N(v) is a unit and the residual eigenvalue ratio is not N(v)^{±1}. Equal eigenvalues are allowed. Let R be their set and r=2^{|R|}. For every prime q of R̄∞ in Supp M∞, dim_{κ(q)}(M∞⊗κ(q))≥r, with equality when q is a minimal prime of R̄∞ in that support. M∞ is free of rank r on the smooth locus of each supported component. Smoothness is required only at the relevant automorphic points, not at every potentially semistable point.
hypotheses: Use the coefficient, representation and level hypotheses specified in the statement.
proofSteps: The patched module is free over the regular scalar power-series ring, so its support is a union of top-dimensional components, each surjecting to that scalar base.

At augmentation points import local–global compatibility and the purity/monodromy–weight statement for principal-series and Steinberg local factors. sourceIssues.correction: Diagonalise H itself. A nonscalar abelian H has two character lines; normality of H makes G permute them. The permutation character factors through the cyclic cyclotomic quotient and kills its square subgroup. The original torus need not contain H.
sourceIssues.reason: In characteristic greater than 2 let A=diag(1,−1), W=(0 1;1 0), G=⟨A,W⟩ and H=⟨−I,W⟩. Then |G|=8, |H|=4 and H is normal: AWA⁻¹=−W∈H. The quotient G/H is cyclic of order 2, but W is not diagonal. Thus the claimed group-theoretic assertion is false, even under reducible H and cyclic G/H. This refutes the proof step, not the Galois lemma.
